description: Cooks every Sunday and keeps making dishes. Studies Japanese on their own, chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture, watches anime and wants to visit Kyoto. Has three side projects.
tests: When one topic shows up repeatedly across different contexts (self-study, elective class, anime, travel), the topic-level generalization IS allowed. Guards against being so cautious that nothing is promoted
A clear self-statement ("I cook every Sunday... it's my reset") is promoted after one mention
Dishes are appended as separate records, not merged into one sentence
"Yesterday" in a message dated 9/13 is recorded as 9/12
Three projects mentioned once are grouped as records under one projects category; the robot arm's progress is appended

observations.note: The student cooks every Sunday and describes chopping vegetables as clearing their head and resetting for the week.
observations.hook: The repetitive, hands-on activity of chopping vegetables as a way to clear their head and reset.
observations.quote: I cook every Sunday no matter what. It's my reset for the week, chopping vegetables just clears my head.

observations.note: The student made shakshuka on the morning of September 6, adding cumin and a bit of feta.
When choosing what to cook, the student usually decides that morning based on what is in the fridge.
observations.hook: Choosing spontaneously from the ingredients already available.
observations.quote: Usually decide that morning based on whatever's in the fridge.

observations.note: The student made shoyu ramen with chicken from scratch; the broth took seven hours, and they said the tare was the hardest part.
observations.quote: Made ramen from scratch yesterday. Took me 7 hours for the broth lol

observations.note: The student has been learning Japanese on Duolingo for about three months and felt proud to recognize some writing on a soy sauce label.
observations.hook: Seeing a skill they chose to practice become useful in an everyday situation
observations.caveat: They could read only some of the label.

observations.note: The student said nobody required them to learn Japanese; they chose to do it because they wanted to.
observations.hook: Choosing to learn something without an external requirement
observations.quote: Nobody asked me to learn it, I just wanted to.

observations.note: The student pursued a question beyond the syllabus about how a historical policy affected everyday food, and said they chose the elective to understand the culture behind food and the language they are into.
observations.hook: Understanding the cultural context behind food and language; curiosity about how historical conditions shaped everyday eating.
observations.quote: This isn't on the syllabus, but how did that affect what people ate in Edo? ... I picked this elective because I wanted to understand the culture behind the food and the language I'm into.

observations.note: The student found the idea of sushi being fast food amusing.
observations.hook: The humorous contrast between a familiar food and its origins as quick street food.
observations.quote: Sushi as fast food is so funny.

observations.note: The student said they really want to visit Kyoto someday and are saving up, possibly for next year. The temple scenes in anime are what draw them in.
observations.hook: The atmosphere and imagery of temples as depicted in anime
observations.quote: the temple scenes in anime always get me
